tagline: Up the Shadowy St. Joe under the cottonwoods.
intro: Forest Highway 50 leaves St. Maries, a sawmill town since 1889, and runs east up the St. Joe River. For the first half the river is deep and still, and steamboat passengers called it the Shadowy St. Joe for the cottonwoods reflected in it. Bald eagles and osprey nest in those cottonwoods and fish the river.

At St. Joe City the water turns shallow, fast and clear and starts running through rapids. Seventy-five miles up, where Road 218 comes in, the highway turns north and climbs 14 miles to the Montana line.

moments.title: Marble Creek
moments.text: Displays here tell how loggers of the early 1900s got white pine out of the Marble Creek drainage and down to the mills on the St. Joe.

moments.title: Avery
moments.text: In the Great Fire of 1910 a backfire built with the help of the Buffalo Soldiers of the 25th Infantry saved Avery, then a division point on the Milwaukee Road.

moments.title: Red Ives Ranger Station
moments.text: Ten miles south of the byway on Road 218, the ranger station named for a red-haired prospector dates from 1935, when the Civilian Conservation Corps built the first roads into the area.
